questions.q: What is a dish made of?
questions.a: One or more ingredients - materials needed to prepare it - like rice, water and salt for cooked rice.

questions.q: Name the ingredients of boiled rice.
questions.a: Rice and water (salt if added for taste).

questions.q: Where do food ingredients come from?
questions.a: From plants and animals - rice from plants, milk and curd from animals.

questions.q: Name five plant sources of food.
questions.a: Rice, wheat, mango, spinach and mustard (seeds, fruits, leaves, stems, roots).

questions.q: Name five animal sources of food.
questions.a: Milk, curd, butter, eggs and meat (also honey from bees).

questions.q: What do animals that eat plants provide us?
questions.a: Milk, eggs and meat - animal products used as food.

questions.q: Name the edible plant parts with one example each.
questions.a: Root (carrot), stem (potato/sugarcane), leaf (spinach), flower (cauliflower), fruit (mango), seed (wheat/gram).

questions.q: Is tomato a fruit or vegetable botanically?
questions.a: A fruit - it develops from the flower's ovary and holds seeds.

questions.q: Why do we eat different plant parts of different plants?
questions.a: Different plants store food in different parts - beetroot stores it in root, sugarcane in stem.

questions.q: What is sprouting?
questions.a: Soaking seeds (like moong or chana) in water till they germinate and sprout small white shoots.

questions.q: Why are sprouted seeds more nutritious?
questions.a: Sprouting increases vitamins (like vitamin C) and makes food easier to digest.

questions.q: How do you prepare sprouted moong at home?
questions.a: Soak moong overnight, drain the water, and leave the seeds wrapped in a moist cloth for a day.

questions.q: How is honey made by bees?
questions.a: Bees collect nectar from flowers, store it in the hive, and fan it into thick honey.

questions.q: Where do bees store honey and why?
questions.a: In hexagonal honeycombs of the hive, as food for the colony.

questions.q: What parts of plants do bees use to make honey?
questions.a: Nectar - the sweet juice inside flowers.

questions.q: What are herbivores? Give three examples.
questions.a: Animals that eat only plants and plant products - cow, goat, deer.

questions.q: Name the food of a cow.
questions.a: Grass, hay and grains - all plant material.

questions.q: Why do herbivores have flat teeth?
questions.a: Flat grinding teeth chew and crush plant food.

questions.q: What are carnivores? Give three examples.
questions.a: Animals that eat other animals - lion, tiger, frog.

questions.q: What do carnivorous animals eat?
questions.a: Flesh of other animals - they hunt or eat other creatures.

questions.q: Which teeth help carnivores tear food?
questions.a: Sharp, pointed canine teeth tear flesh.

questions.q: What are omnivores? Give three examples.
questions.a: Animals that eat both plants and animals - humans, bears, crows.

questions.q: Why are humans called omnivores?
questions.a: We eat plant foods (rice, vegetables) and animal foods (milk, eggs, meat).

questions.q: Name the diet of a crow.
questions.a: Omnivorous - grains, insects, scraps: both plant and animal matter.
